sheet.title: The Arabic alphabet, made simple.
sheet.subtitle: 28 letters · 4 positional forms · dots · non-connectors · Book pp. 1-72
sheet.coreIdea: Letters join **right -> left** in up to **4 forms**, but **6 letters never join the next one**.
sheet.coreIdeaNote: Forms: Beginning, Middle, End, Free. Same body + different dots = a different letter. Learn the sound first, the name later (p. 4).

sections.heading: 2. Six non-connectors: ا د ذ ر ز و
sections.note: They join the letter before them, never the one after: the next letter restarts

sections.note: Count the dots and check above or below

blocks.title: No dots to help:
blocks.text: Daal د is angled and sits on the line; Raaʔ ر curves below it (same for ذ and ز). Laam ل is a tall stroke with a round bowl; Kaaf ك has a flat base and a small inner mark.

sections.heading: 4. Sounds with no English twin
sections.note: Book tip: don't chase the exact sound yet -- link each sound to its shape

sheet.exerciseIntro: Three exercise types: find a missing letter, join letters into words, split words into letters. All are unvowelled -- you work with shapes only.

exerciseTips.title: Start at the right
exerciseTips.text: Every word begins at its right edge.

exerciseTips.title: Spot the six
exerciseTips.text: ا د ذ ر ز و end a joined piece.

exerciseTips.title: Count the dots
exerciseTips.text: Same body, different dots = different letter.

exerciseGuide.task: Choose the letter NOT found in the word, then write the remaining letters
exerciseGuide.method: Read the word right to left and tick off each bracketed letter you find in it. The one with no match is the answer. Watch dot twins such as ص and ض, or ت and ث, or س and ش.

contrast.note: Key 13: اتصالات has ص but not its twin ض

exerciseGuide.task: Join three letters into one word
exerciseGuide.method: Write right to left: first letter in its **Beginning** form, the middle one in its **Middle** form, the last in its **End** form. After ا د ذ ر ز و the next letter restarts (Beginning, or Free if last).

contrast.note: Key 8 is ذهب: since ذ can't join, ه starts fresh

exerciseGuide.task: Join four letters into one word
exerciseGuide.method: Same method; check each letter: does it join to the left? A non-connector inside the word leaves a small gap, not a new word. ة and ى (Chapter 4) only come last.

example.note: Key 2 is كتاب: the last ب stands Free

contrast.note: Key 1 is مسبح: one unbroken piece

exerciseGuide.task: Join five or six letters into one word
exerciseGuide.method: Mark every non-connector first; each one splits the word into pieces. Then write piece by piece: Beginning -> Middle -> End inside each piece, Free for a lone letter.

example.note: Key C20 is مستور: ر after و stands Free

contrast.note: Key D1 is استخرج: breaks after ا and after ر

exerciseGuide.task: Break each word down into its letters
exerciseGuide.method: Go right to left and split at every joint and every gap. Write each letter in its Free form, e.g. a Middle ـمـ is written as م. Words starting with ال: count ا and ل as two letters.

example.note: Key 30: ا س ت س ل م

contrast.note: Key 7: ظلال starts with ظ, but the key prints ض (misprint)

sheet.exerciseFooter: The exercise words are unvowelled on purpose: Chapter 1 is about letter shapes and joining. The vowelled forms on this page are only for reading practice.

front.en: Can it join the NEXT letter (on its left)?

back.en: No · Alif links only from the right (red broken link on the left). The next letter restarts with its Beginning form (or Free if it is the last letter).

front.en: Can it join the NEXT letter (on its left)?

back.en: No · Daal links only from the right (red broken link on the left). The next letter restarts with its Beginning form (or Free if it is the last letter).

front.en: Which 6 letters never join to the next letter?

back.en: ا د ذ ر ز و · Alif, Daal, Dhaal, Raaʔ, Zaay, Waaw

front.en: What form does a letter take right after ا د ذ ر ز و?

back.en: Its Beginning form, or its Free form if it is the last letter: nothing can attach to it from the right.

front.en: Why do د and similar letters show only 2 different shapes for 4 positions?

back.en: They cannot connect on the left, so Beginning looks like Free (د) and Middle looks like End (ـد).

front.en: Why is the last ب written in its Free form?

back.en: ا cannot join to the left, so the ب after it stands alone: بـا + ب.

front.en: Why does ه take its Beginning form here?

back.en: ذ is a non-connector, so ه starts a new piece: ذ + هـب.

front.en: Which letter splits this word into two pieces?

back.en: Alif: كتا + ب. A gap after a non-connector is not a new word.

front.en: Which letter splits this word into two pieces?

back.en: Waaw: مستو + ر, so ر stands in its Free form.

front.en: Green link vs red broken link: what do they mean?

back.en: Green link = the letter can join on that side. Red broken link = it cannot join on that side.

front.en: Which letters of the alphabet have no dots at all?

back.en: أ ح د ر س ص ط ع ك ل م ه و (13 letters)

front.en: This tooth could be 5 letters. Which?

back.en: ب ت ث ن ي -- only the dots tell them apart in the Beginning and Middle forms.

front.en: د or ر: how do you tell them apart?

back.en: Daal (د) is angled and sits on the line; Raaʔ (ر) curves down below the line.

front.en: ذ or ز: how do you tell them apart?

back.en: Both have 1 dot above. Dhaal (ذ) is the angled د shape; Zaay (ز) is the curved ر shape.
ـن is a deep round bowl with 1 dot above; ـب is flat with 1 dot below.
ـف: flat tail, 1 dot. ـق: deep round bowl, 2 dots.
Laam (ل) is a tall stroke ending in a round bowl. Kaaf (ك) has a flat base and a small mark inside.

front.en: ـحـ ـجـ ـخـ: which is which?

back.en: Look for the dot: none = ح (ḥ), below = ج (j), above = خ (kh).
No. ه is English h. ح is ḥ -- the dot under h marks a sound English does not have.
No. س is English s. ص is ṣ, a sound without an English equivalent (dotted s).
No. د is English d. ض is ḍ, a sound without an English equivalent (dotted d).
No. ت is English t. ط is ṭ (dotted t).

front.en: ذ / ز vs ظ: same sound?

back.en: No. ذ is dh, ز is z. ظ is ẓ (dotted z).
No. ك is k. ق is q, its own sound.

front.en: ع vs أ: what is the difference in the book's symbols?

back.en: ع = ʿ, a special symbol for a sound with no English equivalent. أ = ʔ. Two different sounds.

front.en: What does a dot under a transliteration letter (ḥ ṣ ḍ ṭ ẓ) mean?

back.en: The Arabic sound does not exist in English; the dotted letter is the closest English counterpart.

front.en: How should a beginner treat the hard Arabic sounds?

back.en: Don't worry about the exact sound yet. Listen, imitate, and link each sound to its shape.

front.en: How many letters does Arabic have?

back.en: 28 letters

front.en: In Arabic, how are the short vowels written?

back.en: Not with letters: you write the consonants and show vowels with diacritics above or below each letter.

front.en: What does this word mean? (compare عَقْدٌ)

back.en: Necklace. Kasrah under ع. With fatḥah, عَقْدٌ = contract: one mark changes the meaning.

front.en: What does this word mean? (compare عِقْدٌ)

back.en: Contract. Fatḥah on ع. With kasrah, عِقْدٌ = necklace.
At the right edge, moving left. An Arabic book also opens from the right.

front.en: What are the 4 positions (variations) of every letter?

back.en: Beginning, Middle, End, and Free (on its own).

front.en: Which matters more right now: a letter's name or its sound?

back.en: Its sound -- that is what you use to read words. Names are good to know but not strictly necessary yet.

front.en: Which direction do you draw an Arabic letter?

back.en: From right to left, following the red numbered writing guide around each letter.

front.en: Pen and paper or keyboard for learning?

back.en: Pen and paper: writing and linking letters by hand speeds up learning.

front.en: The book shows this word in two calligraphy styles. Same word?

back.en: Yes. Calligraphy can make the same letter look slightly different, especially in the Quran.
